cards.claim: Using interpolation kernels for downsampling without proper anti-aliasing filtering causes visual artifacts
cards.conditions: Image downsampling operations; typical interpolation kernels (bilinear, cubic)
cards.effect: Unspecified visual degradation; industry practice shows this mistake is common
cards.evidence: Qualitative observation of industry practice and recommendations
cards.quote: For instance, even in commercial products we find the mistake of using interpolation kernels for downsampling without the necessary lowpass filtering.

cards.claim: Insufficient spectrum attenuation during downsampling causes 'screen door' effect
cards.conditions: Downsampling with filters that don't adequately remove periodic spectrum repetitions
cards.effect: Visible aliasing artifacts (screen door effect) in output images
cards.evidence: Visual demonstration with example image (Figure 4c) showing the artifact
cards.quote: Another problem occurs when the filters do not remove enough of the periodic versions in the spectrum of the sampled signal. In this case we have the "screen door" effect, as shown in Figure 4 (c).

cards.claim: Linear interpolation kernels applied to downsampling produce DC response errors that oscillate with resampling offset
cards.conditions: Linear interpolation (tent function) used for downsampling; varying resampling offsets; ratio > 1
cards.effect: ~20% oscillation in output values (±10% from ground truth) when offset = 0
cards.evidence: Mathematical analysis with quantified measurements shown in Figure 10-11
cards.quote: In fact, in the latter case, if the resampling offset is zero, then the sampled response will alternate between values that are about 10% too large, and 10% too small, i.e., an oscillation of about 20%!

cards.claim: Different downsampling kernels produce measurably different output quality
cards.conditions: Downsampling by factor 0.6; natural images with fine detail (JPEG2000 'Bike' test image)
cards.effect: PSNR differences of 2-19 dB between different kernels; visual quality varies but all produce acceptable results
cards.evidence: Quantitative PSNR measurements comparing Lanczos (LZ4), Blackman-Harris (BH6), and cubic B-spline (CBS) kernels
cards.quote: The values in the main diagonal show that the images obtained with the kernels and their approximations are indeed very close. The other values are also large, indicating that all those kernels produce good results, but the differences are also clear.

cards.claim: Fast frequency-domain decay in kernels reduces DC response error during downsampling
cards.conditions: Downsampling operations; kernels with fast asymptotic decay in both time and frequency domains
cards.effect: Nearly constant DC response error across all resampling offsets (≤2% error shown in Figure 14-15)
cards.evidence: Frequency response analysis and measured DC response errors comparing proposed kernels to standard interpolation kernels
cards.quote: As explained in Section 5.5 , an advantage of the new kernels is that they present very fast decays on the frequency response, which can make them (depending on the parameters) better for downsizing because of the smaller error on the DC response.

cards.claim: Anti-aliasing (lowpass filtering scaled to the downsampling factor) is theoretically required to prevent aliasing when downsampling
cards.conditions: When resampling factor M > 1 (downsampling); signal spectrum not strictly bandlimited to avoid aliasing condition
cards.effect: Without anti-aliasing filter, aliasing occurs; with proper time-scaled kernel, aliasing is avoided
cards.evidence: Signal theory from sampling theorem; frequency-domain analysis in Section 2
cards.quote: If, on the other hand, we have M > 1, then spectrum of s(t) has to satisfy (15) to avoid aliasing. This can be done by using a time-stretched version as the reconstruction kernel.
